award-0a1f1d1b8505.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The Wings for Val Foundation (WingsforVal.org) proudly honors the life and legacy of Lt. Cmdr. Lyndsay Evans (August 21, 1993–October 15, 2024), a Naval aviator whose leadership, discipline, and pursuit of excellence set her apart. Lyndsay represented a generation of aviators who did not wait for opportunity—they created it. She led from the front, held herself to the highest standards, and earned the respect of those around her through consistency, strength, and integrity. This scholarship honors a leader who set the high bar--and met it. Lyndsay Evans did not rely on intention alone. She showed up prepared, took responsibility, and delivered. Her legacy is one of action, accountability, and quiet confidence earned through hard work. This award seeks to recognize a woman who reflects that same standard—someone who is already putting in the work, who understands what it takes to succeed in aviation, and who will continue to raise the bar for herself and others. The goal is not simply to support a pilot in training, but to invest in someone who will lead, by example, in the next generation of aviation.

award-01f442f53c03.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The Wings for Val Foundation, (WingsforVal.org) honors the life and legacy of Navy Lt. Valerie “Val” Delaney (May 14, 1986–March 11, 2013), a Navy pilot whose courage, character, and passion for flight continue to inspire those who follow in her path. Through this award, the Wings for Val Foundation seeks to support a pilot in training who will carry forward Val’s legacy with purpose, integrity, and determination—someone who will not only take flight but help shape the future of aviation. This award is not just a financial investment—it is a recognition of potential. It is intended for an individual who reflects Val’s determination, resilience, and commitment to something greater than herself. The recipient will represent a legacy of leadership, service, and courage within the aviation community. Women Military Aviators Dream of Flight Scholarship TWO OFFERED – at $3,000 each U.S. SCHOOLS ONLY Women Military Aviators (WMA) seeks to preserve, for history, the important role women have played in creating and supporting the American Spirit through their contributions to flight, aeronautics, and space. These elite bands of women have not only a love of aviation but have put their lives on the line in defense of their country through their military service. WMA is committed to passing this legacy from one generation of women to another and has established an annual scholarship program in support of this commitment. Advocating the love of aviation, WMA offers an annual scholarship to advance a woman in her pursuit of flight ratings at an accredited institution or FAA Approved Part 141 or Part 61 flight school. Over the past 30 years this scholarship has been given to select candidates so that they may pursue opportunities in aviation. Applicants must write about their demonstrated persistence and determination to flight. State ability to complete training at an accredited institution or FAA Part 141 or Part 61 flight school within one year of scholarship award. Identify the school, college, university, Part 141 or Part 61 flight school where training will be completed. Specifically address the program and/or ratings being sought. Address your interest and/or participation in military aviation. Address your financial need. (Center) Mia Corliss 2026 Alaska Airlines, Hawaiian Airlines, Horizon Air Pilot Scholarship

award-1b7e12cc1279.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The ATP CTP course is a prerequisite for the FAA’s highest certificate. This training program will impart conceptual knowledge through academics and consolidate that knowledge through training in a Flight Simulation Training Device (FSTD). The course bridges the knowledge gap between a pilot who holds a private pilot certificate and a pilot operating in an air carrier environment. This program meets the requirements of FAR §61.156. Successful completion of our FAA-approved course makes you eligible to take the ATP Multi-Engine (ATM) knowledge test, which you may take at any testing center. The ATP Certificate Training Program is 7-9 days long, (32 hours) 4 days ground taught by an experienced airline pilot; (10 hrs) 3 days advanced flight simulation training in a Level D Full Flight Sim; (4 hours) 1 day of Level D Flight Training Device as crew; (6 hrs) 2 days of Level D Full Flight Sim (FFS) as crew. This scholarship does not include lodging and transportation. Training must be scheduled to commence no later than one year from award. Cannot be converted to cash value or transferred to any other course or person.

award-0546c2fa9e62.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. award-b9a12b09957d.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. This scholarship is in memory of Bunny M. award-6781caed705a.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. Women in Aviation International (WAI) in partnership with J. Elliot Marketing (Nipomo, CA), offer a $2,500 flight training scholarship in memory of Christine Reed. Christine never completed her flight training. She loved airplanes and loved airports, and she attempted to become a private pilot. Christine passed away unexpectedly at the age of 32 and was never able to complete her flight training. The Christine Reed Memorial Flight Scholarship is open to women ages 16-30 that have soloed within the last six months preceding applying for this scholarship and are working toward their recreational, sport pilot, or private pilot certificate – advanced certificates/ratings may be considered depending the quality of the applicant pool. Applicants must provide a copy of their solo endorsement with the application. Preference will be given to New Jersey, Illinois, and Arizona residents but all applicants will be considered. Fund will be paid directly to the flight school of your choice.

She set both her sights and her standards high. To celebrate her life and accomplishments, the WAI Wright Chapter is offering a $2,000 scholarship to a woman who embodies the qualities that Elisha so splendidly exemplified, and who is seeking to further her aviation career in one or more of the following areas: flight training (any phase); aircraft scheduling or dispatch; aviation management; aviation maintenance or avionics. award-f31bf2ed527a.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. award-c36fdba14b1f.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. In memory of aviation pioneer Esther Noffke, George J. Priester Aviation is awarding one flight training scholarship worth $5,000. Esther’s passion for aviation was evident from a young age. In March 1944, Esther and 48 of her classmates earned their silver WASP wings, officially becoming Women Airforce Service Pilots (WASP). In December 1944, when George Priester bought Pal-Waukee Airport, she began the role of his administrative assistant. She became an integral part of the development and growth of the Chicago Executive Airport. In 2010, Esther was awarded the Congressional Gold Medal for her service with the WASP. Esther’s legacy in the aviation industry is marked by her unwavering dedication and the significant impact she had on the institutions with which she was associated.

award-d7fd424f278f.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The Evelyn Lockwood Greene Memorial A&P Maintenance Scholarship is intended for a woman pursuing a career in aviation maintenance and fabrication who shares Evelyn’s passion for restoring, maintaining, and flying vintage aircraft. This scholarship will fund airframe and powerplant (A & P) certification. Evelyn became an Airframe and Powerplant rated aviation mechanic and went on to achieve Inspector Authorization and Designated Maintenance Examiner status. In her words, she was a “helicopter mechanic by trade,” working for the Honolulu Police and Fire Rescue divisions. She joined the faculty at Honolulu Community College as an Associate Professor of Aviation Maintenance Technology. She worked with many students, helping them achieve their goals. She bought her first plane, a 1969 Cessna 150 and went on to earn private, commercial, and instructor pilot certifications. Additionally, she qualified as one of the only female Reciprocating Flight Engineers in the world, serving as a crew member on a 1951 Douglas DC-6 prop liner used by the Hawaii Oil Spill Response team.

award-01dc5649ad46.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. J. Elliot Marketing of San Luis Obispo County, California offers a $2,342 academic scholarship for community college students in loving memory of Harold Earl Paige. For a man who never thought he’d lived past 30, let alone 40, he lived a fun, full life of 83 years (mostly on his own terms). Though he endured many obstacles along his path, he was steadfast in achieving whatever he set his mind to. As a statistics professor at community college in Chicago, a STEM tutor to elementary students in Illinois, and a certified flight instructor, he helped hundreds along the path to their dreams. This scholarship serves to keep his spirit alive, as well as inspire others to share their passions with the world and find ways to pay it forward. Preference will be given to candidates who have volunteered in aviation and/or STEM-related activities.

award-e8e0a4382e8d.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. award-9049848e68c9.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. award-4ac74a9f17fd.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. award-fd629c83fb3f.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The WAI Washington State Chapter offers a $1,500 scholarship for Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (S.T.E.M.) education in memory of Yukiko Howell. Yukiko taught math, science, and Japanese language for many years at Annie Wright School, a private school in Tacoma, Washington. After obtaining her private pilot certificate, Yukiko taught weekly aviation lessons at her school, including the basics of flying. She advocated aviation in her school lessons, emphasizing math and science proficiency as a means to achieve an exciting aviation career. She used her own flight training and flight experience to motivate her students. Yukiko was a volunteer for the WAI Washington State Chapter scholarship committee and at our local education and outreach events. S.T.E.M. careers include science, engineering, air traffic controller, avionics technician, dispatch certification, aircraft mechanic, meteorologist, educator for S.T.E.M. Applicants must be pursuing higher education toward a S.T.E.M. career or continuing education S.T.E.M. classes, be enrolled in an accredited institution (includes 2- and 4-year colleges, technical institutes, certificate programs), and have experience volunteering in S.T.E.M. or aviation-related events and/or WAI activities in the previous year.
